$comment: The token architecture of resources/css/app.css - PF-199.
Three things are declared here that a stylesheet cannot say about itself:

1. which prefix is which LAYER, and what a layer is allowed to read - the whole architecture is the rule that a component never reads a primitive, and a rule needs the layers to be tellable apart by name;
2. the ROLE every token family stands for, because 'a token may only be added with a stated role' is a review rule and a review rule with nowhere to write the role is a review rule nobody applies;
3. the tokens that deliberately do NOT invert, with the reason, so nobody 'fixes' one later by giving it a dark value.
Both directions are checked: a family here that app.css does not define is as much a failure as a token in app.css that belongs to no family.

primitive.role: A raw OKLCH ramp step. No meaning, no role, and an L% C H triple rather than a colour function, so the same step can be reused at another alpha.

semantic.role: A role a theme answers for. Redefined by every theme and mapped once into @theme, so `text-primary` follows the theme with no `dark:` at the call site.

component.role: A token a component owns, derived from a role or a literal measurement. Never a primitive: a component that reaches past the roles cannot be re-themed, and the theme it breaks is whichever one nobody opened.

scrollbar.owner: The scrollbars of the page shell, the sidebar and the data grid - app.css @layer base, both the standard and the -webkit- syntax.

role_families.background: The page itself, behind every surface.
role_families.surface: A card, a panel, a table - the plane content sits on. The -raised, -sunken, -hover and -selected variants are the same plane in another state.
role_families.surface-container: A tone-based container (Material 3): a contained area one step away from what contains it, rather than lifted by a shadow. -lowest through -highest are those steps.
role_families.on-surface: Text on a surface. -muted is secondary text, -subtle is the quietest text that is still text.
role_families.outline: A decorative line - a card edge, a table rule. -subtle and -strong are the same line with less and more weight. WCAG sets no contrast for these, which is exactly why outline-control is a separate role.
role_families.outline-control: The boundary of something you OPERATE - an input, a select, a checkbox. WCAG 1.4.11 requires 3:1 for it, and a rule refuses a form control whose border is one of the decorative roles.
role_families.primary: The primary action, and the brand's 60% colour. -hover is its hover state, -subtle a tinted container of it.
role_families.on-primary: Text and icons on the primary fill. -subtle is text on the tinted container.
role_families.link: A link in running text, which has to be distinguishable from the text around it without relying on the underline alone.
role_families.accent: The brand teal as a GRAPHIC: an indicator, a sparkline, a chart series. Never text and never a fill under text - white on it is 3.40:1.
role_families.tertiary: A third action weight, below primary: a link-coloured button, the quieter half of a pair. -subtle is its tinted container.
role_families.on-tertiary: Text on the tertiary fill. -subtle is text on the tinted container.
role_families.insight: What the machine proposed - a suggested match, an extracted value, a prediction. Kept apart from every other status so that 'a computer thinks this' never reads as 'this is confirmed'. -subtle is its container.
role_families.on-insight: Text on the insight fill. -subtle is text on its container.
role_families.danger: An error, a refusal, a destructive action. -subtle is its container.
role_families.on-danger: Text on the danger fill. -subtle is text on its container.
role_families.warning: Needs a human: a draft, an exception, an unreviewed import. -subtle is its container.
role_families.on-warning: Text on the warning fill. -subtle is text on its container.
role_families.success: Matched, posted, reconciled - a state that is complete. -subtle is its container.
role_families.on-success: Text on the success fill. -subtle is text on its container.
role_families.focus-ring: The outer colour of the focus indicator, drawn as an outline with a 2px offset.
role_families.focus-halo: The inner colour of the focus indicator, filling the offset gap. Two colours rather than one because no single colour clears 3:1 against every fill a focused control can have - in the high-contrast themes the two constraints have an empty intersection.
role_families.brand-cta: The sign-in action's gradient, which is a brand moment rather than a button: -start and -end are measured separately because text sits over both.
role_families.on-brand-cta: Text on the brand gradient, measured against both ends of it.
role_families.figure: A number. NEUTRAL on purpose - the ink, not a 'good news' green: money is not good news by default. -muted is a figure that is context rather than the answer; -negative is the accounting negative, which also carries parentheses and a sign, because WCAG 1.4.1 means the hue cannot be the only carrier.
role_families.debit: A debit amount in a journal view. The same ink as a figure, declared separately so that a tenant convention wanting them distinguished has a role to change rather than a stylesheet to edit.
role_families.credit: A credit amount in a journal view, for the same reason as debit.
role_families.draft-stripe: The hatch on a draft document. Decoration beside the literal word 'draft', which is what carries the meaning.
role_families.suspense: A figure parked in suspense: real money in the wrong place, which is a warning rather than an error.
role_families.sidebar: The navigation column, which is Midnight Navy in every theme but the high-contrast pair. -raised is a hovered row, -selected the row you are on, -accent the mark on it.
role_families.on-sidebar: Text in the navigation column. -muted is a section heading or a secondary line in it.
role_families.info: DEPRECATED - `info` became `insight` (UX-002). The aliases resolve through the insight roles and are removed after one release.
role_families.on-info: DEPRECATED - the text half of the `info` aliases.

non_inverting.outline-control: A single mid tone (neutral-500) in the light and the dark themes alike, because it is the one line whose contrast is REQUIRED - 3:1, WCAG 1.4.11 - and a mid tone is what clears 3:1 against a near-white surface and a near-black one at the same time. Giving it a dark-theme value would mean choosing between the two ends, and the high-contrast themes do move it because they can afford to. Not an oversight: it was undocumented until PF-199 measured it.
non_inverting.sidebar: The navigation column is Midnight Navy in every theme but high contrast - the brand's 60% colour, and the one surface that identifies the product. It carries light text in the light themes too, which is why its own on- roles exist.
non_inverting.sidebar-raised: The hover state of a row in that column, so it follows the column rather than the page.
non_inverting.sidebar-selected: The row you are on in that column, so it follows the column rather than the page.
non_inverting.on-sidebar: Text in a column that is dark in the light themes, so it cannot be the page's own ink.
non_inverting.on-sidebar-muted: The quieter text in that column, for the same reason.
non_inverting.sidebar-accent: Glacier Teal marks where you are, in every theme including the high-contrast pair: it is the one piece of brand that survives the contrast themes, and it is a graphic rather than text.

literal_colour_exceptions.select:not([multiple]):not([size]): The native select arrow is an inline SVG in a data: URL, and a data: URL cannot read a custom property - so the stroke is a baked hex, once per lightness, and the forced-colours block gives way to the native arrow where even that is wrong. A real defect of its own kind, recorded rather than hidden: the arrow is the one mark in the interface that does not follow the theme, and fixing it properly means a mask-image whose colour is a token.
literal_colour_exceptions..dark select:not([multiple]):not([size]): The dark half of the same baked arrow.
